common_cons: No flagship-grade telephoto zoom except Nothing Phone 3a — expect digital crop on the others
Charging speeds lag behind Chinese flagships across the board
common_pros: All three deliver smooth 120Hz OLED displays that feel flagship-grade in daily use
Battery comfortably lasts a full day for every model tested
Build quality punches above the price — no cheap plasticky feel on any of them
meta_description: Pixel 9a vs Galaxy A56 vs Nothing Phone 3a: real reviewer consensus on camera, battery, updates and value. No fluff, just what matters.

products.best_for: People who want the best camera and longest software support — buy it and forget about upgrading for years
products.name: Google Pixel 9a

specs.Battery: 5100mAh — largest here; PhoneArena measured nearly 20 hours of web browsing
specs.Camera: 48MP main + 13MP ultrawide — fewer lenses than Nothing, but Google's software makes each shot count
specs.Charging: 23W wired + 7.5W wireless — slowest wired charging of the three, but the only one with wireless
specs.Chip: Tensor G4 — same silicon as Pixel 9 Pro, tuned for AI photo processing rather than raw gaming speed
specs.Display: 6.3-inch OLED, 120Hz, 2700 nits peak — smaller than rivals but brightest of the three outdoors
specs.Updates: 7 years of Android + security — unmatched; effective cost is ~$71/year if you keep it the full run
specs.Water resistance: IP68 — the only one you can safely drop in a pool

products.summary: The default recommendation. Tensor G4's computational photography beats everything else here, especially in low light where Night Sight is in another league. Seven years of updates means your $499 stretches further per year than any rival. Trade-offs: 23W charging is slow (full charge takes 1h42m), and the 6.3-inch screen feels small if you're coming from a big phone.

products.best_for: Samsung ecosystem users who want fast charging and a big screen without flagship money
products.name: Samsung Galaxy A56

specs.Battery: 5000mAh — PhoneArena measured ~18 hours browsing, about 90 minutes less than Pixel 9a
specs.Camera: 50MP main with OIS + 12MP ultrawide + 5MP macro — the macro lens is filler; reviewers call it a spec-sheet checkbox
specs.Charging: 45W wired — fastest here; 55% in 30 minutes. No wireless charging
specs.Chip: Exynos 1580 — Samsung's own mid-range silicon; fine for daily use, not a gaming champ
specs.Display: 6.7-inch Super AMOLED, 120Hz, 1900 nits peak — biggest screen here, great for media
specs.Updates: 6 years of Android + security — second best, covers you until 2031-2032
specs.Water resistance: IP67 — survives rain and splashes, not pool submersion

products.summary: The safe pick. One UI is the most feature-packed Android skin here, and 45W charging fills the battery in 1h15m — nearly 30 minutes faster than the Pixel. Six years of updates is excellent. But the camera is the weak link: reviewers note oversharpened, overprocessed photos, especially in low light where it trails the Pixel visibly. No wireless charging.

products.best_for: Design-first buyers who want a telephoto lens and the lowest price — if you upgrade every 2-3 years anyway
products.name: Nothing Phone 3a

specs.Battery: 5000mAh — reviewers couldn't kill it in a day of heavy use; real-world endurance matches the Pixel
specs.Camera: 50MP main + 50MP telephoto + 8MP ultrawide — the telephoto is the standout; no one else has optical zoom at this price
specs.Charging: 50W wired — 50% in 19 minutes, fastest top-up speed here. No wireless charging
specs.Chip: Snapdragon 7s Gen 3 — efficient and smooth; beats Exynos in sustained performance
specs.Display: 6.77-inch AMOLED, 120Hz, 1300 nits — largest screen, but dimmest peak brightness of the three
specs.Updates: 3 years Android + 5 years security — the shortest; fine if you upgrade often, bad if you don't
specs.Water resistance: IP64 — splash-proof only; the weakest of the three, avoid pools and heavy rain

products.summary: The personality pick. At $379 it's the cheapest here, and it's the only one with a real optical telephoto lens — genuinely useful for portraits and distant shots. The Glyph light interface is polarizing but unique. 50W charging is quick. The catch: only 3 years of Android updates (reviewers flag this as the dealbreaker for long-term buyers), and IP64 means it's the least water-resistant — don't take it swimming.
